title: Your Body Makes 4 Million New Cells Every Second 🧬 #shorts
description:
Your body replaces about 330 billion cells every day – nearly 4 million every second. Around 86% of them are blood cells, red blood cells live only about 120 days, and your gut lining is renewed every 3 to 5 days. That adds up to roughly 80 grams of new cells a day, and by count you replace about all your cells every 80 to 90 days. The 'every seven years' idea is a myth – and most brain neurons are never replaced at all.

Sources: Sender & Milo, Nature Medicine (2021), Weizmann Institute of Science, Scientific American, ScienceAlert, Harvard BioNumbers, Live Science

scenes.text: Right now, while you watch this, your body is making about four million new cells. Every single second.
scenes.headline:
4 MILLION
NEW CELLS
PER SECOND

scenes.text: In 2021, scientists at the Weizmann Institute in Israel added up how fast every part of the body renews itself.
The result: about three hundred thirty billion cells are replaced every day.
scenes.label: CELLS PER DAY

scenes.text: Most of them are blood. Eighty-six percent of all new cells are blood cells.
A red blood cell lives about four months. The cells lining your gut? Just three to five days.
All together, that's about eighty grams of brand new you, every single day.
scenes.label: GRAMS PER DAY

scenes.text: By count, you swap out almost all your cells in about three months. Not every seven years. That's a myth.
The twist? Most of your brain cells and the lenses of your eyes are never replaced. They stay with you for life.
